title: Majestic: A Bishop Waiting Move Against a Queen
summary: Keep the queen tied to the king’s cage, then answer each queen defense with a pawn check, bishop mate or exact winning capture.

nodes.question: How can White pass the move without losing the mating threats?
nodes.explanation: Be6 keeps the bishop on the route to b3 while preparing Bd7 if Black pushes b4. The queen must keep preventing mate, but its legal moves cannot preserve the defense.

branches.title: Source defense: block the bishop with the queen
commentary: Begin after ...Qc2, with White Ka2/Bf7/a3/b2 and Black Ka4/Qc2/a5/b5 all retained. The earlier queen sacrifice is outside this proof.
Be6 preserves the diagonal to b3 and prepares a checking answer to ...b4. It is the source’s waiting move; the proof covers every legal Black reply.
Qc4+ checks Ka2 along c4–b3–a2 while blocking the bishop’s route to b3. White must answer the check, and direct Bb3 is unavailable.
b3+ interposes against the queen check and checks Ka4 at the same time. The pawn is protected by Ka2; Black cannot interpose against its adjacent pawn check.
Qxb3+ is the only legal reply. It captures the checking pawn and checks Ka2 again, but reaches an exact seven-piece White win because the bishop can capture the queen.
Bxb3# captures the queen with check. Ka2 protects b3, a3 covers b4, and Black’s a5/b5 pawns occupy the remaining escape squares.
branches.explanation: Bxb3# captures the queen with check. Ka2 protects b3, a3 covers b4, and Black’s a5/b5 pawns occupy the remaining escape squares.

branches.title: Source defense: release the b-pawn
commentary: Compare Black’s only pawn move in the complete later diagram.
Be6 prepares Bd7 with check if the b5 pawn leaves its blocking square.
b4 changes the pawn cage, but White’s king on a2 still controls b3.
Bd7+ checks along d7–c6–b5–a4. The king cannot escape through b3 or b4, and a5 remains occupied.
Qc6 is the sole legal block. The queen interposes on the checking diagonal.
Bxc6# removes the blocker. The bishop checks a4, White’s a3 pawn protects against Kxb4, and the black a5 pawn and white king close the other flights.
branches.explanation: Bxc6# removes the blocker. The bishop checks a4, White’s a3 pawn protects against Kxb4, and the black a5 pawn and white king close the other flights.

branches.title: Independent defense: give check on b1
commentary: Test the queen’s legal checking resource, which is omitted from the source’s concluding two branches.
Be6 leaves Black the choice of queen checks as well as quiet defenses.
Qb1+ checks Ka2 along the adjacent diagonal. The queen on b1 is not protected by Ka4.
Kxb1 legally captures the queen and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. This stops at the checked ending rather than assuming a later conversion.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Kxb1 legally captures the queen and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. This stops at the checked ending rather than assuming a later conversion.

branches.title: Independent defense: guard b3 from d3
commentary: Test another queen placement that prevents an immediate bishop mate on b3.
Be6 maintains both the bishop route and the pawn-check option.
Qd3 guards b3 across the third rank. White can still use the pawn check to force the queen onto the bishop’s diagonal.
b3+ checks with the protected pawn. The black king has no legal flight.
Qxb3 is forced and reaches an exact supported White win.
Bxb3# completes the same protected bishop mate, this time after a different queen defense.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Bxb3# completes the same protected bishop mate, this time after a different queen defense.

branches.title: Independent defense: move the queen far away
commentary: Test a queen move that abandons the b3 defense rather than offering a capture.
Be6 keeps b3 available along e6–d5–c4–b3.
Qh7 is legal, but neither controls b3 nor gives check to the white king.
Bb3# gives the protected adjacent bishop check. No distant queen interposition is possible against that check.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Bb3# gives the protected adjacent bishop check. No distant queen interposition is possible against that check.

exercises.prompt: Why use b3 against Qc4 rather than move the bishop directly?
exercises.answer: Qc4 blocks the bishop’s diagonal. The pawn check forces Qxb3, putting the queen back on a square the bishop can capture.

exercises.prompt: Can Black try a queen check instead?
exercises.answer: Yes. Qb1+ is legal, but Kxb1 captures the undefended queen and leaves an exact winning seven-piece ending.
